<thought>We need to determine the number of CH₃ (methyl) groups in the compound present in the sample. The best way is to retrieve the 13C NMR spectrum of the sample and count the signals that fall in the typical methyl carbon chemical shift range (≈10–30 ppm). This will give the number of distinct methyl carbons, which corresponds to the number of CH₃ groups. We'll request the carbon NMR data.</thought>
